summary: This local feature profiles community outreach programs started by the city's police officers between September 2023 and March 2024. The programs include youth service, cultural exchange, basketball, coffee chats, addiction recovery, tutoring, fitness, and music. Together they aim to build trust and show officers as part of the community rather than apart from it.
one_line: Profile of eight police-led community programs launched in 2023-2024 that build trust through service, sports, education, recovery support, fitness, and music.
key_facts: 'Streets to Service' was launched by the city's Police Department on September 15, 2023; it is the brainchild of Sgt. Michael Rodriguez, a 15-year veteran.
Streets to Service holds Saturday cleanups and youth mentoring, has completed over a dozen projects, and Officer Yolanda Perez led teens in planting a community garden at Mayfield Park.
Officer David Chen started a Bi-monthly Cultural Exchange Workshop on February 21, 2024, after arriving at the precinct in January 2024, to address tensions in Asian-American communities.
The Midnight Basketball League was conceived by Officers Regina Harris and Jacob Torres and launched on October 1, 2023.
The Midnight Basketball League runs every Friday night at the Elmhurst community center court and teaches teamwork, respect, and discipline to teens.
'Coffee with a Cop' was initiated by Officer Anna Moretti, with its inaugural event on November 10, 2023, offering free coffee and informal chats at local coffee shops.
Officer Mark Gonzalez, who has a background in addiction recovery, launched 'Road to Recovery' on December 15, 2023, partnering with local rehabilitation centers.
Road to Recovery trains officers to respond to overdoses and guide victims to support, stressing compassion over criminalization.
Officer Kevin Brooks spearheaded 'Education First' from January 22, 2024, with off-duty officers tutoring at Lincoln Middle School, a struggling school.
Sergeant Linda Thompson started 'Fit for Life' on February 8, 2024, a free weekly workout program at the local gym for residents and officers.
'Harmony Patrol', a musical outreach program, began on March 5, 2024, led by Officer Daniel Kim, an accomplished pianist.
Harmony Patrol performs at local schools, senior centers, and community events, and includes teaching children guitar chords.
